title: Remembering Those Who Prey on the Weak

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Remember what the Amalekites did to you along the way when you came out of Egypt. When you were weary and worn out, they met you on your journey and attacked all who were lagging behind; they had no fear of God. - Deut 25:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls His people to remember what the Amalekites did. When Israel was newly freed from Egypt, weary and worn out, the Amalekites attacked, and they targeted the weakest, those lagging behind, the exhausted and the vulnerable at the rear. It was a cowardly and cruel act. And God notes the root of it, "they had no fear of God." Their cruelty flowed from having no reverence for the God who sees.

This passage shows us that God takes note of how the vulnerable are treated. The Amalekites preyed on the weak and defenceless, and God did not forget it. Those without fear of God often show their character in how they treat the powerless, whether with compassion or with cruelty. God stands as the defender of the weak and the witness against those who exploit them.

This challenges us to examine our own hearts. Do we, out of reverence for God, protect and care for the weak and struggling? Or do we ignore or take advantage of them? The fear of God, a deep reverence for Him, shapes how we treat the most vulnerable around us. Those who truly know God will have hearts tender toward the weak, not cruel. God's own heart is always for the lagging, the weary, and the worn out, and He calls us to reflect that heart. How do you treat those who are struggling and falling behind, and does the fear of God shape your compassion?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you treat those who are struggling and falling behind?
2. Does reverence for God shape your care for the weak?
3. Where can you defend or support the vulnerable this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You defend the weak and see how they are treated. Fill me with reverence for You that overflows in compassion for the vulnerable. Amen.
